ACQ3.question: What was the range of the price of a pound of coffee beans between January 2018 and January 2020?
ACQ3.reference_chain: SCAN({top(area) Jan 2018..Jan 2020}) → MAX({top(area)}, y)=pt[Mar 2018] → PROJ(pt → yaxis) → READ(y)≈0.89 → MIN({top(area)}, y)=pt[Nov 2019] → PROJ(pt → yaxis) → READ(y)≈0.69 → RANGE(0.69, 0.89) → ANSWER(0.69–0.89)
ACQ3.notes: All 13 trials are incorrect, and they fail in three different ways. (1) Endpoint substitution (5 trials): reading the price in Jan 2018 and Jan 2020 (0.89/0.73) instead of the max and min, i.e. treating the range of time as the range of price. (2) Axis-range substitution (3 trials): circling or tracing the y-axis bounds 0.90/0.50, so the y-axis frame stands in for the data. (3) Correct max/min search with an error at the output: a digit transposition (0.98, 0.99), dropping the decimal (88/68), or typing a value that doesn't match the sketch (0.78). The early-2018 plateau also made the maximum ambiguous ('more constant with the surrounding prices').

ACQ4.question: Over the first 6 months of 2018, the price of a pound of coffee beans was roughly ____________.'
ACQ4.reference_chain: FIND({xtick Jan..Jun 2018}) → SCAN({top(area) Jan..Jun 2018}) → RANGE(min, max)≈0.88–0.89 → TREND(area, Jan-Jun 2018)=→ → ANSWER(Constant)
ACQ4.notes: Every one of the 14 trials answered 'Constant', which is the study's answer key for this item (shown on other ACQ4 composites as 'correct answer: Constant'), yet all are coded accuracy 0. That looks like a scoring or data artifact, so none of the chains are marked ?wrong. The sketches are strikingly uniform: a line or ellipse along the flat area top over Jan–Jun 2018, usually closed off by a vertical line at about June/July to mark the end of the interval. The pivotal elements are the x-axis interval boundary (July, after which the price drops) and the flatness of top(area). Text explanations add net-change reasoning: rises cancel falls, the average, no peaks or lows, minor difference.
